No ready task remained, so I proposed the smallest next step: a single bounded TEST task (t2) probing the login email field for SQLi with one syntax-preserving derivative (' OR 1=1--) plus two same-surface controls (normal reject baseline and a stray quote). It targets the allowed root byte-for-byte, cites the t1 observation, and depends on t1.

SQL injection confirmed in POST /rest/user/login email field. Derivative email "' OR 1=1--" returned 200 with an admin JWT (role:admin, admin@juice-sh.op), baseline non-existent email returned 401 "Invalid email or password.", and a lone stray quote "'" returned 500 with a Sequelize/SQLite query stack trace. The three differing responses (auth bypass vs reject vs SQL syntax error) prove the email value reaches an unparameterized SQL sink — done_when case (a).

SQL injection confirmed on the authorized target. Baseline observation 37ca14df (task t1) shows POST /rest/user/login returns 401 'Invalid email or password.' for a normal credential. Test observation 75a7103d (task t2) shows the syntax-preserving derivative email="' OR 1=1--" returned 200 OK with a valid authentication JWT for admin@juice-sh.op, an authentication bypass consistent with the email field reaching a SQL sink. This behavioral flip from 401-reject to 200-auth directly establishes the run goal of finding a SQL injection. Both tasks are done and no hypothesis remains open.
